name: ops
label: Ops
description: One screen for 'is the machine all right?': what the crew ran in the last 24 hours and what failed, token spend, routine health, the WhatsApp and Copilot bridges, the Python apps, free disk, the size of jobs/logs/trash/media, the settings file's age and the last backup. It reads; it does not change anything.

steps: Open Apps > Ops. Runs in the last 24 hours are counted by status, with failures listed by objective; tokens are the sum of prompt+completion for those runs. Services shows WhatsApp, the Copilot bridge and every Python app with its own error. Storage is free disk, the size of jobs/logs/trash/media, the settings file's age and the newest backup.

A failed run links to its transcript in Chat. A Python app that says 'running but not answering' is a live probe, not a stale flag; its log is jobs\apps\<name>.log.err. The Copilot bridge's session expiry is shown, not guessed.
The newest file under backups\ is reported with its age and the total count. No files means no local backup has run on this machine; that is a fact the page states rather than a warning it invents.
fixes: Ops says a Python app is not answering

It is running but its health probe failed: open its page (the first request often restarts it) and read jobs\apps\<name>.log.err. 'needs install' means its requirements have never been installed - install it once from Apps.
The disk figure is for the wrong drive
Every fixed drive is listed; the one holding the app folder is labelled with the repo path. Free space is what Windows reports, not a quota.
Nothing has written to backups\ on this machine. On the box that runs the nightly job the timer is debbiebot-backup.timer; the page only reports what it can see from here.
